mod_sources.key: B58 native national-idea names/descriptions; bounds are a locator envelope for separate sets

english_verification.review_scope: Representative current-Mod opening history and English flavour names; fixed-revision offline English Wiki country stub for Adenica's knightly identity and Greentide destruction; no exhaustive mission-tree audit. Native English idea names/descriptions were compared by localisation key with the current Mod. Wide line ranges locate separately read passages, not exhaustive coverage. No formal validator, build, browser or gameplay test was run.
unresolved: The Wiki country page supports the ancient kingdom's identity and destruction, but does not establish a canonical restoration year, unique predecessor or current formation conditions.
The B58 formation route and late mission reachability were bounded text checks, not a complete playthrough or mission audit.

rationale.campaign_length: The structured local library identifies 54 direct B58 missions, including parallel virtue lines.
rationale.colonization: The pre-formation Adventurer campaign may involve colonisation, but the B58 route focuses on conquest and governance in existing regions.
rationale.complexity: Formation conditions, ten virtues, cavalry infrastructure, event choices and religious-war counters interlock.
rationale.dark_story: The Greentide's destruction, religious suppression and forced conversion cast a shadow, but this is not a sacrifice or extermination story.
rationale.difficulty: The formation gate and the high accumulated-war requirements later make the campaign long; strength has not been play-tested.
rationale.diplomacy: Regent Court relations, contact with Corinites and Cannorian politics provide a diplomatic dimension.
rationale.early_pressure: Another country must first secure Taranton and ten provinces in western Castanor before the B58 route opens.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Mage advisers and a legendary weapon appear, but knights, cavalry and religious politics are clearly more central.
rationale.narrative_density: A fallen ancient kingdom, chivalric virtues, warhorses, court reorganisation and Cannorian religious goals form a complete long arc.
rationale.tall_play: Rebuilding Taranton, the lance school, horse grounds and administrative facilities requires local development, but is not the only loop.
rationale.trade_economy: The treasury and economy must support horse grounds, buildings and the legendary lance; no exclusive trade loop has been confirmed.
rationale.warfare: Restoration conquest, cavalry missions and late religious wars form the main axis, with accumulated-war requirements at the end.

identity.appearance: An ancient kingdom destroyed by the Greentide; current province history shows no B58 territory in 1444, and a qualified country later forms it through a restoration decision.
identity.formation_scope: The normal decision permits formation by several eligible predecessors meeting western Castanor, Regent Court, Escanni culture or Adventurer, Taranton and other conditions.

predecessors.relationship: A special optional predecessor; after hidden de-monsterisation and loyalty conditions, a dedicated event forms B58 and changes the displayed name, so it is not the unique predecessor.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: The Kingdom of Adenica was the birthplace of the common ideals of "knights" and chivalry. When Adenica fell during the Greentide, that shining beacon of honour and chivalry was lost. With Adenica reforged again, we will rise to meet the ideals of our forefather and shine once more. With righteous hearts, our knights will reclaim their former glory as they ride against injustice.

With righteous hearts, our knights will reclaim their former glory as they ride against injustice.

description.text: Adean is the first-born son of Castellos, and the god of honour, justice and chivalry. When our kingdom was founded, and now refounded, our people embraced these ideals in their entirety. To this end, every man, woman, and child holds this pledge in their hearts: "We are the spear of Adean and all he stands for. No matter what evil we face, we shall not falter."

description.text: There is no doubt in our minds that Corin deserved her ascent to godhood for her valiant sacrifice ending the Greentide. Yet this attempted usurpation of the Regent Court shows that perhaps it was truly Agrados reborn, not Corin ascendant, that has declared war upon the gods. The Corinites do not pledge themselves to Corin and her beliefs, but to Agrados. This vile heresy and desecration of both Corin's name and the Regent Court as a whole cannot be tolerated. We must be the spear of Adean once more.

description.text: When Castanor fell, Adenica fought for its sovereignty against the other successor states. It fought to the last as the Greentide brought ruin to Escann. Even when struck down, its spirit continued to fight. And, through fire, blood and steel, Adenica was reforged. Adenners have never feared fighting for what was right and they are ready and willing to continue that fight once more.

description.text: In Adenica, we pride ourselves on our high standards of honourable conduct. It is a core element of our culture and society, second only to our faith. This high level of honour and respect has led to a vastly lower level of corruption, blackmail and abuse of power within our bureaucracy.

description.text: To rule in Adenica, you must prove yourself worthy of rule. To do this, one must obtain knighthood before ascending to the throne. This has been a long standing tradition within our kingdom, and has proven profoundly useful. Our Knight-Kings are known throughout the world for their chivalrous and honourable conduct, and are role models to many rulers and heir-apparents. This reputation has left us in good standing within the global community.

description.text: Our proximity to both the Empire of Anbennar and the reborn realms of Escann have provided us a unique opportunity. We are able to draw on the regulations and innovations of the Western Cannorians, and the military expertise from the Escanni realms. We can leverage this advantage to stay head of the curve, and ensure our ability to protect those in need.

description.text: Even though our clan is very young, its history can be traced back to the early days of the Greentide. When orcs invaded, they dragged their goblin slaves out with them from the Serpentspine. Many of these goblins came riding on the backs of giant spiders. These giant spider riders were a fearsome force; however, they had a major downside. Giant spiders are not native to Escann, so when a goblin lost their mount in battle, it was extremely expensive, if possible at all, to get a replacement. What wasn’t rare to find in Escann were dogs; plenty of stray dogs roamed the now war-ravaged land. Dismounted riders soon began using dogs as replacements, and almost immediately after that, they began breeding them to improve speed and riding capability. As the cohesion of the Greentide started to collapse, many of these now-free dog riders came together and formed the Flying Hound clan.

description.text:
We goblins were nothing but fodder to the Dookanson, used as flimsy meat shields. And while we were slaughtered by adventurer firearms, the orcs mindlessly charged after the first barrage, running over every dying goblin and bringing them to an agonising end.

 Now that we are free, this will no longer be. We will fight as we learned in the darkness of the caverns, cleverly hiding and attacking with poisoned arrows, ambushing enemy leaders and bleeding their armies. This is the way of goblin warfare, and it is the way we will forever follow as long as we are free.

description.text: When news of the Dookanson's death spread, nearly every goblin was ecstatic, but left feeling very uncertain about the future. Not Elgek, though. When word reached his ears, it is said you could just tell he saw opportunity from the look that was shining forth from his eyes and his big grin. Immediately Elgek sounded a rallying cry which amassed many goblins to his side, especially amongst dog riders who eventually dubbed him clanboss of the Flying Hound clan. Unfortunately, Elgek did not turn out to be the great military mind of our time. He ended up blindly rushing us into wars and picking fights wherever he could, damn the consequences. Luckily, we did soon learn that Elgek had a great knack for diplomacy. When enraged foreign diplomats came barging in and demanding answers for his actions, Elgek always knew exactly what to say and how to steer the conversation in his favor. It was hard to stay mad at such a charismatic personality after having a chat with him, and he managed to get the clan out of facing the worst possible consequences many times. Since his passing, the clan has tried to adopt his style of diplomacy going forward.

description.text:
Though still a hostile place with our former captors and adventurers still lurking, Escann is a much more pleasant place to live than the Serpentspine, with its lush forests and serene lakes. Here, we need not fight over any source of food or water for there is plenty for all.

 With this bounty has come changes among the clans. The ancient traditions celebrated in the darkness of the caves are now festivals in the sunlight and under the shadow of ancient ruined temples consecrated to the many gods of mankind. In this beautiful place, we gblins can create something better than our ancient homeland. Perhaps we found a home at last.

description.text:
Escann is not only rich in food and resources, but also knowledge. Among the old human ruins are books, scrolls and all manner of written stuffs that survived the desolation brought by the Dookanson. All as valuable as any other loot.

 However, these texts are written in a language unlike the crude tongue of the Dwarves we came to grudgingly learn. If we are to make use of this treasure we must decipher this language. Fortunately, we goblins are equally cunning and intelligent. To learn this "common" script, we will capture those adventurers who can and force them to teach us the language of humanity, and learn from the knowledge left by those who inhabited these beautiful lands before us

description.text:
With the progressive modernisation of the clans, a new social class is emerging, created by those goblins who are considered within the clan to be the most astute and have the best manners, as well as having managed to adapt more quickly to the language of humanity than their congeners. They are the Naegub.

 Ranging from merchants to negotiators and even diplomats, they act as the link between the clan and the realms of the other civilised races. They are involved in every transaction and negotiation, be they commercial or political, always wringing the most they can for the clan (and themselves). As such, it is a role of great power. Something that garners immense respect, and envy, within the clan.

description.text: Towards the later years of the Greentide, our sense of identity as a people and the culture of our clan truly began to develop. A wave of fanaticism swept across our clan, which took the art of riding beyond the battlefield and into the hands of the average goblin. No longer was a mount restricted to the rich goblin; instead, all could afford to buy a riding dog, and that they did. Mounted dog races became the most popular and common sport in our lands. Many goblin clothiers began expanding their work to include fashion for dog mounts. One could not go anywhere within our domain and not see a goblin without his ride; the two were inseparable! Joined at the hip! To be a goblin of the Flying Hound clan was to be a goblin and your dog mount. This came full circle, as it was clear that most goblins within our society wouldn't do anything without a mount, and most recruits refused to even go into battle while on foot.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid this route if you do not want to meet a formation threshold first, dislike late accumulated-war goals or do not want a forceful single-faith narrative.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Conquer in western Castanor to form B58, then pursue virtues, horses and restoration in parallel before expanding through Cannor with knights and court politics.
player_overview.overview: Adenica is not a 1444 starting country: first use an eligible Adventurer or Escanni state to reclaim Taranton, then restore the ancient knightly kingdom. The long mission tree develops warhorses, chivalric virtues, hunts and tournaments while reorganising the Regent Court. Cavalry expeditions rebuild Escann, but the player must decide whether protecting the weak can coexist with an aggressive programme of religious unity.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy knightly kingdoms, cavalry, noble oaths, restoration and long religious-political campaigns.
signature_features: Virtue missions track progress and drive the Chivalric Nobility and Mortal Court reforms.
Hunts, tournaments, horse breeding and the legendary lance create a sustained cavalry-development route.
Restoration in Escann leads into Adean and Regent Court politics across Cannor.
player_overview.tagline: Restore the knightly kingdom on the ruins of the Greentide and return Adean's warhorses to Escann.

reasons: A clear restoration story for an ancient knightly kingdom.
Virtues, oaths, hunts and warhorses form a distinctive cavalry loop.
Court and religious politics sustain a long second half.
warnings: The formation conditions must be completed first.
Some late missions require a very high accumulated war count.

positive_indicators: Chivalric justice explicitly requires protecting the weak.
Chivalric charity requires giving back to orphans and vulnerable groups.
Administrative missions establish courts and town halls to handle subjects' grievances.
values.rationale: Chivalric justice, charity, protection of the weak, courts and public services improve dignity and public good; the later religious objective seeks to eliminate rival faith polities, and some events directly change the religion of orc and half-orc areas, lowering personhood and restraint. Conquest, monarchy, noble hierarchy and religious propagation are not scored by themselves; exact coercive outcomes remain partly uncertain.
red_flags: Late missions require Cannor to have no Corinite or Ravelian countries.
Events can directly change the religion of orc and half-orc areas.
Restoration and court order may override the autonomy of dissenting communities.
